chunks.title: About PSERC
chunks.text: The Plateau State Electricity Regulatory Commission (PSERC) is the state electricity regulator for Plateau State, Nigeria. The Plateau State Electricity Regulatory Commission is an independent regulatory authority charged with regulating electricity operations in Plateau State. We are committed to building a commercially viable, fair and sustainable electricity market that serves every resident. Vision focus: An investor-friendly framework with an efficient market structure that meets the needs of Plateau people for safe, adequate, reliable and affordable electricity.

chunks.title: PSERC Mandate
chunks.text: Core mandate of PSERC: To establish a stable legal, commercial and technical regulatory framework for the provision of reliable, safe and affordable electricity to residents of Plateau State.

chunks.title: PSERC leadership and pioneers
chunks.text: PSERC leadership: His Excellency Caleb Manaseh Mutfawn — Governor of Plateau State; Amb. Bagudu M. Hirse — Chairman / Non-Executive Commissioner; Managing Director (to be announced); Barr. Sunday Panwal — Non-Executive Commissioner Legal; Mark Daiei — Executive Commissioner, Finance & Administration; Engineer Julius Agati — Executive Commissioner, Engineering Services and Safety.

chunks.title: How to contact PSERC
chunks.text: Contact PSERC using the Get in Touch form on the official website. Share your name, email and message.

chunks.title: Electricity Act 2023 and state regulation
chunks.text: Nigeria’s Electricity Act 2023 enables States to establish State Electricity Markets and SERCs. Plateau State enacted the Plateau State Electricity Law, 2024 to establish PSERC.

chunks.title: What is PSERC?
chunks.text: PSERC means Plateau State Electricity Regulatory Commission — independent regulator for electricity operations in Plateau State.

chunks.title: Consumer protection and complaints
chunks.text: PSERC focuses on consumer protection and fair market rules. Use the website contact form for billing or service concerns.

chunks.title: Licensing and investors
chunks.text: PSERC provides an investor-friendly framework. Licensing is governed by the Plateau State Electricity Law, 2024 and Commission instruments.

chunks.title: PSERC documents and regulations
chunks.text: Under Resources → Documents, Regulations (#/instruments/regulations), Codes (#/instruments/codes) and Forms & Manuals (#/instruments/manuals), PSERC publishes Business Rules, Captive Power Generation Regulations, Customer Service Standards and Protection Regulation, Licensing Regulations, Mini Grid Regulations, Tariff Methodology Regulation, Draft Grid Code (Version 03), Draft NESIS Regulations 2025, comment sheets, Mini-Grid Schedules 1–15, and Who Does What under the Electricity Act 2023. Anyone may read documents on the website. Downloading requires signing in to the PSERC Portal. The chatbot does not download files.

chunks.title: Business Rules
chunks.text: The PSERC Business Rules set out Commission processes for market participants. Read them under Resources → Documents. Sign in to download. The chatbot cannot download files.

chunks.title: Captive Power Generation Regulations
chunks.text: The Captive Power Generation Regulations govern captive power generation in Plateau State. Read them under Resources → Documents. Sign in to download.

chunks.title: Customer Service Standards and Protection Regulation
chunks.text: The Customer Service Standards and Protection Regulation sets standards and protections for electricity consumers in Plateau State. Read it under Resources → Documents. Sign in to download.

chunks.title: Licensing Regulations
chunks.text: The Licensing Regulations set rules for applying, holding and complying with PSERC licences. Read them under Resources → Documents. Sign in to download.

chunks.title: Mini Grid Regulations
chunks.text: The Mini Grid Regulations set the framework for mini-grid operations in Plateau State. Related Schedules 1–15 are under Forms & Manuals. Read regulations under Regulations or Resources → Documents. Sign in to download.

chunks.title: Mini-Grid Schedules 1–15
chunks.text: PSERC publishes Mini-Grid Schedules 1–15 as Word templates under Forms & Manuals: exclusive development agreements, registration and permit applications, monitoring templates, HSE, technical requirements, network asset use fee methodology, complaints resolution, tripartite and customer contracts, asset handover, tariff model, and hosting-capacity confirmation. Sign in to download. The chatbot does not download files.

chunks.title: Tariff Methodology Regulation
chunks.text: The Tariff Methodology Regulation sets the methodology for electricity tariff setting and related reviews. Read it under Resources → Documents. Sign in to download.

chunks.title: Draft Grid Code Version 03
chunks.text: The Draft Grid Code (Version 03) is the Grid Code for the Nigerian Electricity Transmission System. It covers general conditions, organisation and objectives, review processes, monitoring and testing, connection conditions, operating code, scheduling and dispatch, and related transmission system rules. View it under Regulatory Instruments → Codes. Download requires signing in to the PSERC Portal. The chatbot does not download files.

chunks.title: Draft NESIS Regulations 2025
chunks.text: The Draft Nigerian Electricity Supply and Installation Standards (NESIS) Regulations 2025 set standards for engineering designs, installations, commissioning and maintenance of electric power systems, made under the Electricity Act 2023. View under Regulatory Instruments → Codes. Download requires signing in. The chatbot does not download files.

chunks.title: Who Does What under the Electricity Act 2023
chunks.text: Who Does What under the Electricity Act 2023 explains institutional roles: Federal Ministry of Power; Plateau Electricity Regulatory Commission (PSERC); Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO); and Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN). Read at /services/who-does-what. Download the DOCX after signing in.
